_comment: Deprecated APIs and dependencies, with their modern replacements. Only entries whose 'match' strings actually appear in the project being migrated are injected into a prompt, so the model is never handed advice about APIs the code does not use. Nothing here tells the model to keep the original libraries - it is free to choose a better one. The minimum supported Android API level is declared by config/MigrationPolicy (APOLLO_MIN_SDK, default 29 = Android 10); entries must not hedge about older releases - anything at or below that floor is available unconditionally.

migrations.deprecatedSince: 2018 - the Android Support Library was superseded by AndroidX and receives no updates
migrations.guidance: Replace every android.support.* import with its androidx equivalent, e.g. android.support.v7.app.AppCompatActivity -> androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity, android.support.v4.app.Fragment -> androidx.fragment.app.Fragment.
ActionBarActivity was replaced by AppCompatActivity. Extend AppCompatActivity instead.

Replace the startActivityForResult + onActivityResult request-code pair with a launcher registered at construction time: private val launcher = registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.StartActivityForResult()) { result -> if (result.resultCode == RESULT_OK) { ... } }, then call launcher.launch(intent). Add androidx.activity if the module does not already depend on it.

Replace AsyncTask with a coroutine: lifecycleScope.launch { val result = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { work() }; updateUi(result) }. doInBackground becomes the withContext block, onPostExecute the code after it.

migrations.modern: ViewModel + coroutines (and Room for database access)
migrations.guidance: Loaders are deprecated. Move the data loading into a ViewModel exposing StateFlow/LiveData, backed by a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO.
The framework Fragment class is deprecated. Use the AndroidX fragment library instead.
android.preference.* is deprecated. Use androidx.preference.PreferenceFragmentCompat hosted in an AppCompatActivity.
The implicit-Looper Handler constructor is deprecated because it silently picks the current thread's Looper. Pass the Looper explicitly: Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).
Override of onBackPressed is deprecated. Register a callback: onBackPressedDispatcher.addCallback(this) { ... }.
The theme-less Resources.getColor/getDrawable overloads are deprecated. Use ContextCompat, which resolves against the context's theme.
The single-argument Html.fromHtml is deprecated. Use HtmlCompat with an explicit flags argument.

migrations.modern: An inline ProgressBar, or a custom dialog
migrations.guidance: ProgressDialog is deprecated because it blocks interaction. Show a ProgressBar in the layout instead.
NetworkInfo is deprecated. Query NetworkCapabilities, or observe connectivity with registerNetworkCallback.
The raw-duration vibrate(long) overload is deprecated. Build a VibrationEffect instead.
The Apache HTTP client was removed from Android. Use HttpURLConnection for simple calls, or OkHttp/Retrofit.
Boxed primitive constructors are deprecated for removal. In Kotlin just use the literal or .toInt()/.toLong() - never construct a boxed type explicitly.
Class.newInstance() is deprecated because it silently propagates checked exceptions. Use getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance().

migrations.deprecatedSince: Java 8 introduced java.time; many java.util.Date methods are deprecated outright. java.time is native to Android from API 26.
migrations.guidance: Replace java.util.Date/Calendar/SimpleDateFormat with java.time (LocalDate, LocalDateTime, Instant, DateTimeFormatter). java.time is part of the platform from API 26, so at the target minimum SDK it is available directly - no desugaring, no ThreeTenABP, no fallback to the legacy types.
